additional_info.subject: ID0465776-DC/Si-D/IT-[Multi] OCPP connection goes online and offline CRM:00314000254
additional_info.body:
Dear colleagues,
I am following up our conversation in regards of router connectivity to OCPP lost and the customer that is performing several reboots on several chargers.
Yesterday we discussed about a possibility to manually configure in the Teltonika webUI an automatic reboot when the connection to internet is lost.
This could be an option, we could try to activate it on few chargers and monitor the behavior in the upcoming days. The goal would be for the router to reboot itself and re-establish the network connectivity without having the customer reboot the chargers on their hand.
I discussed the topic this morning with R&D and they confirmed me there is no side-effect to manually configure this autoreboot in the router.
To configure the autoreboot, it can be done in #3 different ways:
Locally on the charger by connecting to the router via ETH cable.
Remotely from HQ via ssh
Remotely from your side with the remote debug tool. This would be the best option, as you would be independent to perform such ocnfigurations.
To do it, you have to:
Connect to the webUI router XF4
Go to System > Maintenance > Autoreboot
In the section Ping/Wget Reboot Settings click on Add
Enable: On. Type: Ping, Host to Ping: 8.8.8.8, Select the interval, select the number of counts that the router tries to ping before rebooting.
It is possible also to change the action: in the line "Action if no echo is received", you can decide either to restart the whole router, or restart the internal modem, or restart the mobile connection. On this, you can try on different chargers and compare which action is more effective.
Hope I provided you with enough information. Please let me know if you need support, and we can schedule a remote session together.
With kind regards,

additional_info.subject: Status Update
additional_info.body:
Between 09.02.2026 and 10.02.2026, Configured the autoreboot on XF4 routers on all chargers of IPlanet (see list).
Latest findings show that, two main root causes were identified:
Weak internet connection, which should be mitigated by the autoreboot
Missing pong from server during websocket ping. This behavior should be addressed by the backend itself.
As per agreed with Valerio and Giuseppe, we will close this ticket after the configuration of autoreboot on all routers.
A new ticket might be created in the future to run a new investigation based on new figures provided by IPlanet after mitigation actions.
